answer: Rewards vest over many epochs instead of paying instantly, and each identity's payout weight grows only through sustained useful work. Flash-farmed sybils collect mere slivers before forfeiting most unvested earnings when abandoned or slashed - a karst field of hollow accounts, riddled like limestone, that never accumulates. Reputation settles like a river depositing sediment: slow, compounding, hard to fake. An attacker must bond capital per identity and keep every account productive for months, so the cost of running the farm exceeds its harvest; cheating burns deposits like saffron,
